questions: Are you experiencing a tremor or shaking in your hands?
Is the tremor worse when your hands are at rest?
Do you have any stiffness or slowness of movement?
Have you noticed any changes in your handwriting?
Do you have any trouble with balance or walking?
Does the tremor get worse when you try to perform an action like drinking from a cup?
Is the tremor worse when you are anxious or stressed?
Have you noticed the tremor improving after you drink alcohol?
Does anyone in your family have a similar tremor?
Are you currently taking any medications?
Is the tremor present only in one hand or both hands?
Does the tremor involve your head or voice?
Does the tremor worsen when you try to hold a specific posture, like holding your arms out in front of you?
Do you have any history of thyroid problems?
Do you drink a lot of caffeine?
Is the tremor a fine, rapid shaking?
Is the tremor a coarse, slower shaking?
Does the tremor improve or worsen completely?
Is the tremor constant or intermittent?
Do you have any weakness in that hand?
orders: Full neurological examination focusing on cerebellar signs
Serum thyroid function tests (TSH, T3, T4)
Serum electrolytes including calcium and magnesium
served: deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses
gait observation including turning and doorways
MRI brain - midbrain (hummingbird sign, midbrain-to-pons ratio)
MRI brain - putamen (atrophy, rim sign, hot cross bun, SWI hypointensity)
MRI brain - white matter and ventricles (small-vessel disease, ventriculomegaly)
